title: Beyond vibe checks: A PM’s complete guide to evals
subtitle: How to master the emerging skill that can make or break an AI product
summary: As AI products become increasingly complex, mastering evaluations (evals) is essential for product managers. Evals provide a systematic way to measure the effectiveness of AI systems, ensuring they meet user expectations and deliver value. This guide outlines various approaches to writing effective evals, emphasizing their importance in the development and continuous improvement of AI products.

title: Why AI evals are the hottest new skill for product builders | Hamel Husain & Shreya Shankar (creators of the #1 eval course)
summary: In this episode, Lenny Rachitsky discusses the importance of evaluation (eval) skills for AI product builders with experts Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar. They explain how effective evals can significantly improve AI applications by systematically measuring performance and iterating on feedback. The conversation also addresses common misconceptions about evals, the integration of AI in the eval process, and the need for product managers to engage deeply with their data to enhance product quality.

title: Why experts writing AI evals is creating the fastest-growing companies in history | Brendan Foody (CEO of Mercor)
summary: Brendan Foody, CEO of Mercor, discusses the unprecedented growth of his company, which has rapidly scaled from $1 million to $400 million in revenue in just 16 months. He emphasizes the critical role of 'evals' in the AI landscape, which are essential for measuring model capabilities and driving advancements in AI technology. Foody also highlights the emerging job opportunities created by AI, countering the narrative of job displacement and suggesting that the future of work will involve humans collaborating with AI to enhance productivity.

title: The 100-person AI lab that became Anthropic and Google's secret weapon | Edwin Chen (Surge AI)
summary: In this conversation, Edwin Chen, founder and CEO of Surge AI, discusses the innovative approach his company has taken to build a successful AI data company without relying on venture capital. He emphasizes the importance of high-quality data and the need for AI models to be optimized for meaningful objectives rather than superficial metrics. Chen expresses concern about the current trajectory of AI development, arguing that many labs are prioritizing engagement over genuine advancements that could benefit humanity.

title: Al Engineering 101 with Chip Huyen (Nvidia, Stanford, Netflix)
summary: In this episode, Chip Huyen shares her insights on building successful AI products, emphasizing the importance of user feedback and practical application over merely keeping up with the latest AI trends. She discusses the challenges companies face in leveraging AI effectively, the distinction between pre-training and post-training models, and the significance of data preparation in AI applications. Huyen also highlights the evolving role of AI engineers and the future of AI in organizational structures, advocating for a balanced approach to innovation and productivity.
